code:
cd ~/cs357-work        # a git repository, with a GitHub remote

docker run -it --rm \
  --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  -v "$PWD:/workspace" \
  -w /workspace \
  --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  course-agent
description: The docker run that gives the container exactly one directory and nothing else, with the flags that bound what it can reach.

steps.description: This mounts one directory into the container and nothing else. The page says the container sees your project because you mount it, and sees nothing else because you do not.
`cd ~/cs357-work` enters the project, which is a git repository with a GitHub remote, so every change is one you can read and revert.

`docker run -it --rm` opens an interactive container that is deleted on exit, so an experiment cleans up after itself. `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` makes `host.docker.internal` resolve on Linux, where Docker Engine does not provide it for free.
`-v "$PWD:/workspace"` is the only door: the current directory is mounted at `/workspace`. `-w /workspace` makes that directory the agent's world from the first keystroke.
`--cap-drop ALL` and `--security-opt no-new-privileges` remove kernel capabilities the agent has no use for.

steps.answer: they were never in the container to begin with
steps.question: The page says `--rm` deletes the container on exit, and your files survive because of what?

title: Mounting One Directory
